title: St Giles Church, Imber: future events (Remembrance service, carols, New Year open days)
what_it_contains: Imber church site lists 2026-27 events: Remembrance service Sat 7 Nov (convoy from Vedette Post 2 at 10:25, Last Post 11:00); Festival of Carols Sat 12 Dec, ticket only, GBP 10, max 4 per application, Bratton Silver Band; New Year open days 31 Dec and 1 Jan 11:00-16:00, road open 08:00-18:00. States: 'We negotiate directly with the Ministry of Defence to arrange Open Days and other events'; MoD may withdraw access at short notice.
why_relevant: Model for a fixed yearly calendar of events inside a live range, negotiated by a small volunteer church group; convoy entry from a single gate is the same pattern the Army could use for the Nathu Dada fair.
found_via: WebFetch after WebSearch 'Imber village open days 2025 church service'

title: Thousands to make rare visit to abandoned Imber village (Imberbus 2026)
what_it_contains: Imberbus Day 15 Aug 2026; up to 30 Routemaster buses; 2025 event raised GBP 36,956.20 from tickets, given to charities incl. keeping St Giles church open; started 2009 by bus-industry volunteers; fares GBP 10 adult / GBP 2 child.
why_relevant: Shows a one-day bus event inside a training area can carry thousands and pay for upkeep of the one surviving building. Direct model for a 'Nathu Dada fair bus' from resettlement villages.
found_via: WebSearch 'Imberbus 2025 routemaster raised money visitors' then WebFetch

title: Imber Village in Colour (private tribute website)
what_it_contains: Tribute site 'published and funded by a resident of Warminster'; colourised photos of villagers and buildings, online village tour by location (Bell Inn, cottages, church, farms), history, protest records, access roads and open days, a Tyneham comparison page. States about 16,000 people visit Imber each year.
why_relevant: Closest analogue to 34gaon.com: one volunteer, one site, photo tour by building/location. Also a counter-example: no family-contribution mechanism, no oral histories.

title: Imber (Wikipedia)
what_it_contains: Evacuated 1943 (about 150 residents, 47 days' notice), told they could return in six months; 1961 rally of 2,000+ and a public inquiry that ruled against return; MoD must allow access 1-50 days a year (reduced to about 3 in late 2010s due to trespass); annual service on Saturday nearest St Giles' Day (1 Sept); carols since 2009; church vested in Churches Conservation Trust 2005, restored by 2009; Imberbus since 2009; last Imber-born villager buried there 5 Jan 2023.
why_relevant: Access rules came out of protest + inquiry, not goodwill; a saint's-day service anchors the calendar, as Asoj Krishna Navami does for Nathu Dada; burial of a former villager inside the range is a precedent worth asking about (samadhi / devli rites).

title: Explore the history of Imber: two free exhibitions at The Athenaeum, Warminster
what_it_contains: Snippet: exhibition 'Imber: The Ghost Village - A walk through the past' with historical maps, archive material and personal family memories through photography, dedicated to the families; open 16-23 August, weekday mornings, free. Page returned HTTP 503 to WebFetch.
why_relevant: Model for a low-cost exhibition in the nearest town timed with the access day (e.g. Lunkaransar or Chhatargarh during the fair week).

title: Tyneham: where time stopped in 1943 (Dorset Online Parish Clerk site)
what_it_contains: Volunteer Online Parish Clerk site (Dorset OPC network, published by one volunteer). About 50 family surname pages (A-Z), transcribed parish registers 1694-1942, censuses 1841-1921 and the 1939 Register, evacuation records and timeline, gravestones, wills, war dead, emigration; visitor pages per building (The Row, church, school, farm) and 'off-limits' places inside the range.
why_relevant: Best structural template for 34gaon family pages: one page per family (gotra) linked to transcribed census rows and a list of places inside the range. Our census tables 1951-1981 can feed the same structure.

title: Lulworth range walks and Tyneham village access times 2025 (MoD, GOV.UK)
what_it_contains: MoD publishes a yearly calendar of open weekends and stand-down periods (Christmas, Easter, 25 Jul-31 Aug 2025 etc.); range-walk gates open about 16:30 Friday after firing and stay open to 08:00 Monday; Tyneham gate 09:00 to dusk; school and church exhibitions 10:00-16:00 on non-firing days; a recorded phone line for status.
why_relevant: Shows an army can publish a fixed yearly access calendar tied to its own firing programme. Something to ask for: a published date for the Nathu Dada fair and any other permitted visits.

title: Tyneham (Wikipedia)
what_it_contains: About 225 residents evacuated Dec 1943; 1948 compulsory purchase; public access began 1975 after complaints (weekends and August); church and school preserved as museums/exhibitions; the last surviving former resident died aged 100 in May 2025 after a last visit in 2024.
why_relevant: 27 years from eviction to regular access; exhibition in the old school is the model for a 'schoolroom' page or a physical display in a resettlement school.

title: Fighting for Tyneham (Dorset Life, Dec 2013)
what_it_contains: Snippet: Tyneham Action Group founded at a public meeting in Dorchester in May 1968, supported by Lilian Bond (author of 'Tyneham: A Lost Heritage', 1956).
why_relevant: The campaign group + one memoir book pattern; the 1956 memoir is on archive.org (tynehamlostherit0000bond).

title: STANTA tour report (Mundford Parish Council)
what_it_contains: Parish council tour of the Stanford Training Area: 110 residents on two coaches with an Army guide; St Mary's church and battle-area sites; GBP 366 raised for STANTA charities; tours are arranged infrequently by the Army.
why_relevant: A village panchayat (not an NGO) can ask the Army for a guided coach tour; the scale (2 coaches) fits a first Ram Nagar / Krishna Nagar trip.
found_via: WebSearch 'Stanford Training Area church visits former residents' then WebFetch

title: Stanford Training Area (Wikipedia)
what_it_contains: Villages West Tofts, Sturston, Langford, Stanford, Buckenham Tofts, Tottington evacuated 1942; access only with Army permission, a limited number of tours a year and on compassionate grounds for former residents or relatives; regular summer visits and a carol service at West Tofts church; Tottington church roof clad in blast-proof sheeting.
why_relevant: 'Compassionate access for former residents and relatives' is an explicit category the 34 gaon families could ask for (e.g. to visit a family devli or well).

title: Grwp Epynt marks 85 years since clearance with donation to hospital
what_it_contains: Grwp Epynt (graziers, SENTA training-area officer, Epynt Way, a Facebook memories group 'Atgofion Epynt', Menter Brycheiniog a Maesyfed, Royal Welsh Show) ran the 85th anniversary: open day at Sennybridge with an avenue of slates bearing the Welsh names of the displaced farms; bus tours of about 30,000 acres with Army permission and sponsorship for about 300 visitors incl. descendants (chapel, school, Drovers Arms); unveiling of a slate listing all those displaced and a tree planting at the Epynt Centre; June concert; school drama 'Iorwerth o'r Epynt'; logo mugs and tithe-map reproductions sold to fund a permanent memorial; sponsor paid for map printing.
why_relevant: Strongest single precedent: a coalition that includes the Army's own range officer got bus tours inside a live range for descendants. Name slates = our village-name stones; tithe-map reprint = our 1955 AMS / 1961 census map reprint.

title: Event marks anniversary of forced displacements of Welsh-speaking community (Nation.Cymru)
what_it_contains: 30 June 2026 storytelling evening 'Colli Epynt / The Epynt Story' by storyteller Euros Lewis, drawing on stories gathered from former residents; 220 people from 52 farms displaced 30 June 1940.
why_relevant: A fixed anniversary date + a storyteller evening costs little; for us: 1987 possession / 1986 notification date.

title: The Epynt Way Association: latest
what_it_contains: Volunteer association maintaining the 80 km permissive route round the Sennybridge range; MoD funded its guidebook; annual EDDUM 50-mile ultra run; memorial stone and tree for its founder (Sept 2023); visitor centre open year-round regardless of firing.
why_relevant: A perimeter route (not inside the range) can be a permanent, safe heritage product. Transfer: a signed 'parikrama' of resettlement villages and range-edge villages, not the range itself.

title: Epynt Way (Wikipedia)
what_it_contains: Permissive bridleway about 80 km created by the Ministry of Defence in 2004 round the perimeter of the Sennybridge Training Area; for walkers, cyclists, riders; keeps clear of firing ranges.
why_relevant: The Army itself built the heritage route; precedent to cite in a request to the Army.

title: Epynt clearance (Wikipedia)
what_it_contains: About 200 people from 54 farms and a pub evicted 1940; farmhouse Disgwylfa refurbished, reopened 2009 as Canolfan Epynt (Epynt Centre) with a plaque of farm names and inhabitants of 1940, start of the Epynt Way; 'Cofiwch Epynt' slogan.
why_relevant: Army-owned building turned into a small memory centre at the range edge.

title: Community Voices: The Protect Kaho'olawe 'Ohana celebrates 50 years
what_it_contains: PKO founded after the 4 Jan 1976 landing; 1980 Consent Decree (Aluli v. Brown) made it recognised steward with monthly access for cultural, religious, subsistence and educational purposes; bombing stopped 1990; island returned to the State 1994; KIRC set up 1993; five generations of stewards trained; annual Makahiki; monitors 600 cultural sites and 3,000 features.
why_relevant: The legal key was a religious practice (Makahiki) that the Navy had to accommodate. Parallel: Nathu Dada fair and Pir Baba Kanolai as recognised religious access.

title: Palapala 'Aelike Kahu'aina: Stewardship Agreement KIRC and Protect Kaho'olawe 'Ohana 2024-2035
what_it_contains: Signed agreement effective 26 Jun 2024 to 25 Jun 2035. States the 'Ohana ran public access for more than 25,000 persons 1980-2024 without major injury or fatality from UXO; the 'Ohana submits an 'Access Safety and Logistics Plan'; KIRC gives UXO and access-guide training; parties meet each December to review the year and fix next year's access dates; persons accessing may be deemed state volunteers.
why_relevant: A ready template for a written, renewable access arrangement: yearly safety-and-logistics plan from the community, training by the land manager, a fixed annual review meeting. Useful as a model letter to the Army for the fair.

title: KIRC volunteer information
what_it_contains: Volunteer trips: about 12-15 people per group, two groups a month, four days, USD 200 access fee incl. boat from Maui, mandatory one-hour orientation, group affiliations preferred due to demand.
why_relevant: Small, supervised, fee-paying groups with a compulsory safety briefing; the scale a live-fire area can tolerate.

title: Makahiki ceremonies on Kaho'olawe usher in season of renewal (HPR)
what_it_contains: 20-60 people each year; boats leave Maui 03:00; gear swum ashore; five-day ceremony; parents bring children, one practitioner training his son as fifth-generation keeper of protocols.
why_relevant: Transmission to children happens by taking them to the ceremony; the fair day should carry a children's role (e.g. youngest family member reads the village name).

title: Key legal documents pertaining to the Kaho'olawe Island Reserve
what_it_contains: Index of legal documents incl. the 1980 Consent Decree (Navy and PKO), Title X of Public Law 103-139 (return 1994), HRS 6K. Snippet: the decree gave PKO 10 calendar days each month for religious and cultural practice (figure from snippet, not verified on the decree text).
why_relevant: Primary legal texts of the best-documented access settlement between a displaced people and a military range.

title: Vieques Struggle: A Digital Video Archive (Georgia Tech)
what_it_contains: Omeka site with OHMS (Oral History Metadata Synchronizer): 107 hours of video testimony recorded in Vieques in 2004; interviews, transcripts, topic tags, gallery, timeline; undergraduate students digitise, transcribe and annotate as coursework.
why_relevant: Working example of Omeka + OHMS for oral histories of a military-range community; and of using a university course as free labour for transcription.
found_via: WebSearch 'Vieques Navy 1941 expropriation displaced families memory' then WebFetch

title: From sugar plantations to military bases: the US Navy's expropriations in Vieques, 1940-45 (Ayala & Bolivar)
what_it_contains: Snippet: Navy expropriated about 26,000 acres 1941-43, evicting over 3,000 people to a central relocation zone; barrios Punta Arenas, Llave, Mosquito disappeared; 89% of people on 27% of the land.
why_relevant: Scholarly method: reconstructing vanished barrios from land and census records, as we did for 1951-1981 census villages.

title: Puerto Ricans expel United States Navy from Culebra Island, 1970-1974 (Global Nonviolent Action Database)
what_it_contains: Snippet: seven months of marches, sit-ins and blockades from summer 1970; protesters tried to build a chapel on Flamenco Beach inside the range where a church had been demolished; Navy left 1975.
why_relevant: Religious building inside a range as the focus of a claim; parallels the temples at Khiyana/Manera.

title: 80 Jahre TUePL: 42 Doerfer mussten weichen (ORF Niederoesterreich)
what_it_contains: Allentsteig/Doellersheim training area: about 40 villages, about 7,000 people resettled 1938-41; yearly All Souls' commemoration in the Doellersheim Peace Church; association 'Verein Freunde der alten Heimat' organises, Austrian Army cooperates; 200+ attended the 80-year event in 2018; unexploded ordnance limits access.
why_relevant: 80 years on, a small association + army cooperation keeps one annual day; exactly the scale 34 gaon can sustain.

title: Truppenuebungsplatz Allentsteig (Wikipedia DE)
what_it_contains: About 6,800 people from 42 communities, 6 hamlets, 10 mills evacuated June 1938-Dec 1941; since 1981 the square, ruined church and graveyard of Doellersheim accessible; church rededicated 1986 as Friedenskirche; a museum in Allentsteig.
why_relevant: Access corridor to one sacred site inside a still-active range, granted decades later.

title: Truppenuebungsplatz Hohenfels: vor 70 Jahren begann Vertreibung (Onetz)
what_it_contains: 1951 expansion displaced 3,218 people (villages incl. Lutzmannstein, Pielenhofen, Schmidheim, Pondorf); annual Heimattreffen (home reunions) in Lutzmannstein, Schmidheim, Pielenhofen and the Enslwang church fair; memorial stone.
why_relevant: Reunion days organised per former village, held in or near the old site, 70 years on.

title: Wintermarsch im Sperrgebiet: die verlassenen Doerfer im Uebungsplatz Hohenfels (Onetz)
what_it_contains: Reservists' winter march (about 80 people) through Pielenhofen and Lutzmannstein arranged by a liaison officer; US Army provided bus transport; former residents are invited every two years to their old village for a church service and traditional meal.
why_relevant: Explicit precedent: a foreign army hosting former residents every two years with a service and a meal inside an active training area.

title: 70 Jahre US-Truppenuebungsplatz Hohenfels: als Doerfer verschwanden (nordbayern)
what_it_contains: 1937-38: about 1,622 people from 60 settlements relocated; 1951 western expansion about 6,000 ha; timeline March-Nov 1951; resettlement of 152 farms. Written by a local liaison officer/historian.
why_relevant: Local-historian-as-bridge model: a person trusted by both army and villagers writes the history.

title: Ausstellung '30 Jahre Konversion rund um die Doeberitzer Heide' eroeffnet
what_it_contains: Snippet: exhibition on the former training area (villages Doeberitz and Ferbitz abandoned); concept by three volunteer local historians of Dallgow and Gross Glienicke; area now a nature reserve after army left.
why_relevant: Mostly a nature-conversion story (range closed); weak transfer, but shows local historians carrying the memory.

title: With Jharkhand CM nod, Netarhat Firing Range to become history (Avenue Mail)
what_it_contains: CM approved not renewing the Netarhat Field Firing Range notification (range from 1964, extended 1999 by Bihar to 2022); about 39 revenue villages of Latehar plus Gumla affected; Jan Sangharsh Samiti since 1994 with annual 22-23 March protests; claim that satyagraha stopped annual firing practice; PESA / Gram Sabha argument.
why_relevant: The only Indian field-firing-range case found with a sustained community organisation, a fixed annual gathering and a documented outcome. Different situation (notified, not acquired; Fifth Schedule).
found_via: WebSearch 'Netarhat field firing range Jan Sangharsh Samiti' then WebFetch

title: Netarhat ke Tootwapani mein sankalp sabha ka aayojan (Prabhat Khabar)
what_it_contains: Snippet: Committee formed Dec 1993; every year on 22-23 March thousands from notified villages gather at Tutwapani; 2025 sankalp sabha held.
why_relevant: An annual date-fixed gathering sustained 30+ years by villagers themselves; Hindi-language press covers it every year.

title: Netarhat field firing range mamla: toote vaadon ke tees saal (The Caravan, Hindi)
what_it_contains: Hindi long-form history of the Netarhat protest (not opened).
why_relevant: Good Hindi narrative model and a source for how an Indian range movement documented itself.

title: State, forest and Adivasis at crossroads: Netarhat field firing range and contestations over rights (Int. J. Human Rights 25:7)
what_it_contains: Academic article on Netarhat range and rights (abstract only).
why_relevant: Scholarly framing for Indian field firing ranges and displacement; possible citation for 34gaon background page.

title: Rehabilitation of Pong Dam oustees in Rajasthan pending for over 50 years (Land Conflict Watch)
what_it_contains: Pong Dam (1974) displaced 30,000+ families from 339 villages; 16,352 families eligible for IGNP land in Rajasthan; by 1992 only 9,196 allotments, 6,658 cancelled; SC judgment 1996 set up oversight committee; Dec 2018: 12,027 allotments, 8,009 in possession; WP(C) 1140/2020; March 2021: 6,355 families unsettled. Forum: Pradesh Pong Bandh Visthapit Samiti Rajasthan. No memory mechanisms recorded.
why_relevant: Closest Indian parallel in the same canal colony (IGNP, Bikaner/Jaisalmer/Ganganagar): allotments, cancellations, decades of pending cases (compare 148 MFFR cases pending 2025). Shows what a Samiti + SC petition achieved and did not.
found_via: WebSearch 'Pong Dam oustees Rajasthan IGNP' then WebFetch

title: Himachal dam evacuees wait 50 years for rehabilitation (IndiaSpend)
what_it_contains: 8,000 families still waiting; 72% of early allotments cancelled; barren plots without roads, power or water; 2008 inspection found land unirrigated; standing committee created 2008 then inactive; SC committee met 17+ times since 1996; climate shock quote (15-25 C vs 40 C+).
why_relevant: Evidence of how a displaced group in the IGNP area lost land to cancellations and encroachment; the team can compare with MFFR allotments in Chhatargarh, Khajuwala, Pugal.

title: List of 830 Pong Dam oustees eligible for review of murabba allotment applications (DC Kangra)
what_it_contains: District publishes a named list of 830 oustees whose murabba applications are eligible for review (not opened; contains personal names).
why_relevant: Precedent for a district office publishing a case-by-case pending list; the MFFR 148 pending cases could be requested in the same form (via RTI), but the site must not republish names.

title: Launch of Management Information System for Pong Dam oustees at Kangra (NIC Informatics)
what_it_contains: Snippet: NIC software lets oustees apply online via DC (Relief and Rehabilitation) Kangra; applications sent online to Rajasthan government for murabba allotment. Page 503 on fetch.
why_relevant: An official online tracker for a displaced group's land cases exists in the same IGNP context; a model to ask the Bikaner Collectorate / Colonisation dept for MFFR cases.

title: Rajasthan Colonisation (Allotment and Sale of Government Land to Pong Dam Oustees ... in the IG Canal Colony) Rules, 1972
what_it_contains: Rules governing IGNP land for Pong oustees. Download attempt reset by peer; a human should save the PDF.
why_relevant: Comparable rule-set to whatever governed MFFR allotments in the IGNP colony; legal track should compare.

title: Forgotten oustees: Bilaspur still struggles for justice decades after Bhakra Dam (ETV Bharat)
what_it_contains: Old Bilaspur and 354 villages submerged 9 Aug 1961; about 12,000 families (about 52,000 people); 270 still waiting for plots; committees: All-Party Bhakra Displaced and Affected Committee; 27-28 temples not renovated; poem 'Nau August ki Shaam' by a former MLA; no formal annual events.
why_relevant: Negative example: 65 years with committees but no structured memory practice; the temples surfacing each winter are the only 'open day'.

title: Ek Thi Tehri: a city once submerged still breathes (ETV Bharat)
what_it_contains: Every 31 July (2004 submergence date) former residents gather in Dehradun and light lamps at 'Ek Thi Tehri', a model/replica of the old town made in 2007 by a local craftsman; Tehri Smriti Manch proposes a larger replica near the lake; elders tell children the layout.
why_relevant: Indian precedent for an annual memory date plus a physical model of the lost place in the town where the displaced now live. A 3D model / relief map of one 34-gaon village is doable.

title: Hirakud Dam oustees await rehabilitation and compensation (Land Conflict Watch)
what_it_contains: Snippet: 325 villages, about 26,501 families; Hirakud Budi Anchal Sangram Samiti leads claims; 1 Aug 2024 over 200 beneficiaries got land pattas at Kurla village; temples (Padmasini) emerge when water falls.
why_relevant: Shows pattas still being issued 70 years later after organised pressure; same slow-case pattern as MFFR.

title: Jeevanshala: the Life Schools (Narmada Bachao Andolan)
what_it_contains: Snippet: from 1991-92 NBA ran schools in Sardar Sarovar submergence villages; about 5,000 students passed out; now 9 residential jeevanshalas (7 Maharashtra, 2 MP).
why_relevant: A displaced-people's movement turning into an education institution; for 34 gaon the transferable piece is a local-history module, not a school.

title: Sustaining a social movement through infrastructural followup: NBA's schools for life (Social Movement Studies)
what_it_contains: Article on how NBA sustained itself through jeevanshalas after losing the dam fight.
why_relevant: Evidence that memory survives when attached to a running service (school, fair) rather than to a campaign alone.

title: Island villages between Kosi embankments neglected after Bihar floods (Mongabay India)
what_it_contains: Snippet: about 380 villages, 9.88 lakh people between embankments (2011); Kosi Nav Nirman Manch campaigns for rehabilitation.
why_relevant: Weak transfer (live flooding, not lost villages); listed because the brief asked.

title: BaTonga Museum, Binga
what_it_contains: Snippet: museum opened September 2004 on Lake Kariba shore to promote Tonga culture; Tonga (about 57,000) displaced by Kariba Dam late 1950s; Basilwizi Trust and Binga Development Association organise claims.
why_relevant: Small community museum in the resettlement district, 45 years after displacement.

title: Beyond the Kariba Dam induced displacements: the Zimbabwean Tonga's struggles for restitution
what_it_contains: Academic study of Tonga restitution claims, organisations (Basilwizi Trust).
why_relevant: Comparative case of second-generation advocacy.

title: Three Gorges Probe: oral histories
what_it_contains: Collection of oral histories of Three Gorges migrants (1.3 million relocated since 1993), e.g. compensation disputes.
why_relevant: Shows oral histories focused on compensation are a legitimate genre; our interviews should also ask about land and payment, not only culture.

title: From 'Living in History' to 'Ghost Town': Hasankeyf's lost social values (Heritage & Society 19:2)
what_it_contains: Study of social values lost when Ilisu Dam flooded Hasankeyf (2020) and residents were moved to a new town without participation.
why_relevant: Warns that moving monuments without people's stories loses the social value; relevant to any temple relocation idea.

title: Capel Celyn (Wikipedia)
what_it_contains: Flooded 1965 for Liverpool's reservoir; 48 of 67 people lost homes; 'Cofiwch Dryweryn' (Remember Tryweryn) slogan; 50th anniversary 2015.
why_relevant: A two-word slogan painted on a wall became a national memory symbol; cheap and durable.

title: MIRPUR VR (Social History Society)
what_it_contains: VR reconstruction of Mirpur villages submerged by Mangla Dam (280+ villages, 110,000+ displaced; 70% of British Pakistanis of Mirpuri heritage), co-created with diaspora, from community voices, archives, mapping and architectural reconstruction; small-grant funded; premiered Migration Matters Festival 2023.
why_relevant: Diaspora-led reconstruction of a lost place from memories; a lighter 34gaon equivalent is a 2D village sketch-map drawn with elders.

title: Record oral histories (1947 Partition Archive)
what_it_contains: Free 2-hour online workshops since 2012; must pass 80% of summary questions to get portal access; field packets and questionnaire; submission of first interview within one month through an online portal with metadata.
why_relevant: The 'citizen historian' method: short free training + standard questionnaire + upload portal. Copy for 34gaon youth volunteers.

title: Story Scholars South Asia (1947 Partition Archive)
what_it_contains: Stipends: Rs 10,000-15,000 (6-month track) or Rs 16,250-27,500 (3-month) in standard areas; 60 interviews required; must already be a Citizen Historian.
why_relevant: Real Indian cost benchmark: about Rs 170-460 per recorded interview in stipend.

title: The 1947 Partition Archive (Wikipedia) + mission page
what_it_contains: 12,000+ video oral histories (June 2025) from about 5,000 cities and villages in 17 countries; 1,000+ certified Citizen Historians, about 300,000 volunteer hours; 18,000 workshop participants; 2024: 100 volunteer interns, 16 paid DOHA interns.
why_relevant: Scale reference and proof that volunteer training converts at about 5% (1,000 contributors of 18,000 trained).

title: The 1947 Partition Archive on Google Arts & Culture
what_it_contains: Partner page with online story exhibits (e.g. 'Women during Partition').
why_relevant: Google Arts & Culture requires an institutional partner; 34gaon cannot join directly but could supply content through a partner (e.g. a university or state museum).

title: Mukurtu CMS FAQs
what_it_contains: Free open-source Drupal-based CMS for Indigenous heritage with cultural protocols and Traditional Knowledge labels; costs are hosting and IT; managed hosting via Reclaim or Mukurtu Hosting (WSU); free training by web conference; updates about every 12 weeks.
why_relevant: Best fit if families want some items visible only to the community (e.g. women's songs, family photos). Needs a server and a technical volunteer.

title: Get Mukurtu
what_it_contains: Snippet: basic Organizational Shared Hosting through Reclaim Hosting about USD 100/year recommended for small sites.
why_relevant: Cost reference (about Rs 8,500/year).

title: Omeka.net pricing
what_it_contains: Snippet: plans from free to USD 1,200/yr; older listing: Basic free 500 MB, Plus USD 49/yr 1 GB, Silver USD 99/yr 2 GB.
why_relevant: Cheapest hosted archive option; but our static site already does most of this.

title: Mobile Vaani: a voice-based community media network for social development (IIT Delhi / Gram Vaani)
what_it_contains: IVR on missed call: users call, get called back free, record and listen to voice messages by keypad; no smartphone or data needed; 100,000+ monthly active users, 10,000 calls/day across Bihar, Jharkhand, MP.
why_relevant: A proven way to collect voices from elders without smartphones, fit for low literacy; the missed-call model keeps cost with the project, not the caller.

title: Thirty years later, a museum wants to change the way we look at the survivors (Remember Bhopal Museum)
what_it_contains: Survivor-curated museum opened Dec 2014 in a small rented room; about 50 oral testimonies in Hindi; survivors gave objects; curated by an oral historian with a survivors' committee; only individual donations; survivors on staff.
why_relevant: Indian proof that a one-room, community-curated museum with 50 testimonies is enough; also shows the funding risk.

title: About the project (Indian Memory Project)
what_it_contains: Since 2010: curated online archive of family photographs sent by the public, each with the family's own story; accepts images up to 1991.
why_relevant: Format for a 'one photo, one story' page; our 1991 cut-off is natural (the villages ended 1987).

title: Palestine Open Maps: about
what_it_contains: Search and download historical maps and spatial data; 2,000+ historical and present localities; hundreds of map sheets from the 1870s; side-by-side old/new comparison; 3D.
why_relevant: Exact model for our naksha page: 1955 AMS and 1961/1971 census maps side by side with today's satellite, a searchable list of vanished places.

title: iNakba: new interactive app documents destroyed Palestinian villages (Haaretz)
what_it_contains: Snippet: Zochrot app (2014) lays destroyed villages on Google Maps/Waze to navigate there; users upload photos; testimonies attached.
why_relevant: Map pins + user photos per lost village; our site can do this with a static map and a WhatsApp intake.

title: Kheer Bhawani Mela 2025: Kashmiri Pandits begin pilgrimage amid tight security (Deccan Herald)
what_it_contains: Snippet: displaced community's annual return to shrines; convoy of 60 JKRTC buses flagged off by the Relief Commissioner (Migrants) from Jammu; security, boarding and lodging arranged by administration.
why_relevant: Indian precedent of the state running buses and security so a displaced community can reach its shrine once a year. Model for asking district administration (not only the Army) to run buses to the Nathu Dada fair.

title: People's Collection Wales: about
what_it_contains: Snippet: national site since 2010 where anyone uploads photos, recordings, stories; supported thousands of community heritage projects; offers oral history training.
why_relevant: A state-run community upload platform; India has no equal; closest is the team's own site.

title: India-Malaysia joint exercise Harimau Shakti 2025 concludes at Mahajan Field Firing Range (ANI)
what_it_contains: Headline/snippet only: bilateral exercise held at MFFR in December 2025.
why_relevant: Evidence that MFFR is an active, high-profile range (incl. foreign armies); limits any open-day idea to what the Army already permits.
found_via: WebSearch 'Nathu Dada mela Khiyana Mahajan field firing range army 2025'

title: Russia-India Indra 2025 drills kick off at Mahajan Field Firing Range (TASS)
what_it_contains: Headline/snippet only: Indra 2025 joint drills at MFFR.
why_relevant: Same: range in continuous use; access must be negotiated around the Army's exercise calendar (as Lulworth publishes).

title: Tribune Ludhiana, 7 Aug 2001: farmers of nine villages protest evacuation for Halwara air force firing range
